headline_marked: BNP weighs seasoned leaders for [[next president of Bangladesh]]
headline: BNP weighs seasoned leaders for next president of Bangladesh
summary: Following Mohammed Shahabuddin's resignation, the BNP is consulting senior leaders to find a candidate who is politically acceptable and free of controversy.
details: Following the resignation of Mohammed Shahabuddin, the ruling BNP is discussing potential candidates for the next president of Bangladesh.
Prime Minister and party chief Tarique Rahman is consulting senior colleagues to identify a seasoned leader who is politically acceptable and free of major controversy.
Among the names surfacing in internal conversations are BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, and Standing Committee members Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain and Nazrul Islam Khan.
Former Dhaka University professor and economist Dr. Mahbub Ullah is also under consideration for the role.
Mirza Fakhrul is seen as a strong candidate due to his long-standing leadership role and support among civil society and the younger generation.
However, some within the party are oppose choosing a serving or former bureaucrat, arguing the president should be a senior BNP leader who understands the party's history.
The final decision rests with Tarique Rahman, who will hold further consultations with the BPN Standing Committee and senior leaders.
Under the constitution, a presidential election must be held within 90 days of a vacancy arising through resignation, death, or removal.
caption:
Who will be the next president of Bangladesh? The BNP is weighing several seasoned leaders for the role.

Following the resignation of Mohammed Shahabuddin, the ruling BNP is discussing potential candidates for the next president of Bangladesh.

Prime Minister and party chief Tarique Rahman is consulting senior colleagues to identify a seasoned leader who is politically acceptable and free of major controversy.

Among the names surfacing in internal conversations are BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, and Standing Committee members Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain and Nazrul Islam Khan.

Former Dhaka University professor and economist Dr. Mahbub Ullah is also under consideration for the role.

Mirza Fakhrul is seen as a strong candidate due to his long-standing leadership role and support among civil society and the younger generation.

However, some within the party are oppose choosing a serving or former bureaucrat, arguing the president should be a senior BNP leader who understands the party's history.

The final decision rests with Tarique Rahman, who will hold further consultations with the BPN Standing Committee and senior leaders.

Under the constitution, a presidential election must be held within 90 days of a vacancy arising through resignation, death, or removal.

headline: 60kmph winds forecast: 7 regions on storm alert in Bangladesh
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has issued a warning for squally winds and thunderstorms across several southern and eastern districts.
details: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has forecast squally winds reaching speeds of 45 to 60 kmph across seven regions of the country.
The warning, issued on Saturday, July 25, is effective until 1:00 PM today. It covers Khulna, Barishal, Patuakhali, Noakhali, Comilla, Chattogram, and Cox's Bazar.
In addition to the strong winds, these areas are expected to experience rain or thunderstorms.
Due to the weather conditions, river ports in the affected regions have been advised to hoist signal number one.
